History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
54-year-old male with untreated hypertension and hypercholesterolemia presents with 2-hour sudden-onset central chest pressure (7/10) with associated dyspnea, light-headedness, nausea, and left shoulder/arm discomfort; physician arranged immediate ambulance transfer for suspected acute coronary syndrome.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Central chest discomfort described as “pressure, like someone sitting on my chest.”  
• Onset/duration: Sudden onset while gardening; ongoing for “a couple of hours.”  
• Severity/progression: Constant; rated 7/10 at onset and currently.  
• Character: Pressure/discomfort rather than sharp pain.  
• Location/radiation: Mid-chest; radiates to left shoulder and arm; no radiation to right arm, back, or head.  
• Associated symptoms:
  – Shortness of breath (SOB); unchanged since onset; exertional SOB for several weeks when climbing stairs or walking uphill.  
  – Light-headedness.  
  – Nausea without vomiting.  
  – No dysphagia, no change in bowel or bladder habits.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: None reported; discomfort occurred at rest after gardening, persists at rest; no medications taken.  
• Pertinent negatives: No right arm pain, no back pain, no radiation to head, no dysphagia, no GI or urinary complaints.  
• Review of systems otherwise not discussed.

Past Medical History:
• Hypertension – untreated (no medications).  
• Hypercholesterolemia – untreated.  
(No other chronic illnesses reported.)

Medications:
• None.

Allergies:
• Not documented. (missing)

Social History:
• Smoking: Yes (amount/frequency not documented).  
• Alcohol: Not discussed.  
• Recreational drugs: Not discussed.  
• Lives with wife; normally performs light household activities but limits exertion due to breathlessness.  
• Gardening every two weeks.

Family History:
• Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
(No in-person examination performed; telehealth only.)  
• Vitals: Not obtained.  
• No physical findings documented.

Investigations:
• None performed prior to call; EMS and hospital evaluation pending.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Suspected acute coronary syndrome (ACS) / myocardial ischemia  
  – Central chest pressure, radiation to left shoulder/arm, SOB, nausea, cardiovascular risk factors (HTN, hyperlipidemia, smoking).  
  Plan:  
    • Advised immediate EMS activation; ambulance arranged to patient’s home.  
    • Instructed patient to remain calm, sit upright, sip water as needed, avoid exertion.  
    • Expected ED evaluation with ECG, cardiac enzymes, continuous monitoring, IV access, oxygen, possible antiplatelet/anticoagulant therapy per protocol.

Issue 2: Dyspnea with exertion and baseline exercise intolerance  
  – Chronic progressive SOB on stairs/hills; possible cardiac or pulmonary etiology.  
  Plan:  
    • Will undergo work-up in hospital (cardiac evaluation, chest imaging, labs).  
    • Follow-up with primary care/Babylon physician after hospital discharge.

Issue 3: Cardiovascular risk factor management (HTN, hypercholesterolemia, smoking)  
  Plan:  
    • To be reassessed post-acute event.  
    • Anticipate initiation of antihypertensives, statin, and smoking-cessation counseling after stabilization.

General plan items:  
• Physician will arrange follow-up appointment once hospital course is known.  
• Patient advised to inform wife and prepare essentials for hospital visit.

• No prior cardiovascular evaluations documented (e.g., lipid panel, BP readings).
